# Falsifier verdict — F-428 P12.13 (CODE pass)

## Experiments

> **Experiment 1 (independent denominator):** I counted `auto == true && correct == false` records in both fresh traces with a standalone Python script; I expected 57 debug / 74 batch and `other=0`; that is exactly what I got (`records=2410 autoWrong=57`, `records=2114 autoWrong=74`; atom paths only `ranker|override`, 4 multi-atom batch lines each with an `accepted` atom). Claim 1's *counts* hold.

> **Experiment 2 (re-run vs recorded):** I re-ran both census commands and `pairs` at HEAD and byte-diffed all four outputs against the recorded TSVs/summaries; I expected identical; `diff` reported no differences (`ALL-FOUR-IDENTICAL`, `PAIRS-IDENTICAL`), and `pairs` independently re-derives its denominator: P12.7 `census-debug.tsv` has exactly 44 `blocker=window ∧ route∈{compound,other}` rows, all present in the fresh trace. Claims 5 and 6's "matches a fresh re-run" hold.

> **Experiment 3 (guards):** I synthesized a `set=sealed` trace in `/tmp` and ran the CLI; I expected exit 1, refusal on stderr, nothing on stdout; got `exit=1`, `stdout bytes=0`, `refused: set 'sealed' (D-029 allows debug|batch only) at line 1.` Missing file: `exit=1`, `stdout bytes=0`. `grep -c 'Hosting environment'` on census stdout = 0. Claim 4 holds.

> **Experiment 4 (the break — synthetic ladder through the production entry point):** I wrote `/tmp/p1213-falsify/edge.jsonl` with five hand-built lines whose correct class is known, and ran `dotnet run --project tools/LetUsCook.AutoWrongCensus -- census /tmp/p1213-falsify/edge.jsonl`; I expected `pack-unit-state × curated` (jar, Canned key), `row-choice-tier × ranker` (can, both rows Canned, Survey vs Branded), `other + missingField actualDataTypes` (empty `actualDataTypes`), and `compound-head-lost × ranker` (multi-atom, accepted atom third); **all five came back `compound-head-lost`** (sites correct: curated/reuse/ranker/ranker/override). An unknown atom `path` line correctly exits 1 with the refusal and empty stdout.

> **Experiment 5 (contamination on the real traces):** I scanned every `compound-head-lost` row for whether any key-head token beyond the first appears in the rawText (evidence a head word was actually dropped); I expected most to show one; **27 of 29 batch rows and 5 of 16 debug rows show none**. Indisputable cases: `Flour` (accepted row *identical* to key row, `compound-head-lost`), `1 piece onion` (accepted == key, `compound-head-lost`), `300 g beef` / `180 g beef` (accepted "Beef, ground" vs key "Beef, chuck, roast" — cut choice, not head loss), `1 piece boiled egg` ×6 (accepted state `None` vs key `Cooked` — the brief's own `state-mismatch` shape, stamped `compound-head-lost`), `20 g coriander` ×4. Conversely a *genuine* head-loss line — `1/4 cup chopped water chestnuts`, parsedName `water`, key head `waterchestnut chinese` — is classified `sibling-food × override` and missed by the bucket it exists to count.

> **Experiment 6 (§2a mutation inventory, 17 sites, one at a time, `git checkout` restore each):** table below; 14 RED, **3 survivors**.

| # | Site | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | `KeyHeadPhrase` stop (`CarriesStateToken`) | never stop | RED (5) |
| M2 | `PackUnitRegex` | drop `jars?` | RED (2) |
| M3 | pack-unit rule | drop key-must-be-Canned term | **GREEN — survivor** (traces unchanged) |
| M4 | compound rule | `keyHeadPhrase.Length >= 2` → `>= 1` | RED (3) + traces move |
| M5 | compound rule | drop `parsedNameTokens.Length == 1` | RED (4) |
| M6 | compound rule | drop first-word equality | RED (2) |
| M7 | state-mismatch | `!=` → `==` | RED (7) |
| M8 | missing-tier → `other` | delete branch | RED (3) |
| M9 | `SiteOf` ranker | swap reuse/ranker | RED (5) |
| M10 | `SiteOf` curated | delete branch | RED (3) |
| M11 | `ChooseAtom` | always `Atoms[0]` | RED (1) |
| M12 | `IsOverrideKey` | drop the `(` fold | **GREEN — survivor** (traces unchanged) |
| M13 | runner filter | `!record.Auto` only | RED (1) |
| M14 | pairs route filter | widen to all routes | RED (1); pairs 45 → 73 rows |
| M15/M16 | set refusal / missing file | (probed live via Experiments 3 + named tests) | RED |
| M17 | `TierRank` | reverse order | **GREEN — survivor**; real debug summary flips `key higher=2 accepted higher=1` → `1/2` |
| M18 | site-empty refusal | (probed live, Experiment 4) | guard works |

## Findings

**1. `work` — the `compound-head-lost` rule measures key-description composition, not head loss.** `AutoWrongClassifier.cs` fires it on `keyHeadPhrase.Length >= 2 && parsedNameTokens.Length == 1 && parsedName == keyHeadPhrase[0]`. Since `KeyHeadPhrase` runs to the first *state* token, any single-token parser name equal to the key's first token fires it — including when the rawText contains only a unit plus the whole name (`Flour`, `1 piece onion`, `300 g beef`) and the accepted row is *identical* to the key row. 27/29 batch and 5/16 debug rows of the bucket (39% of the batch trace) are mislabelled; the true classes are `state-mismatch` (boiled-egg rows), `sibling-food`/tier/qualifier (beef/coriander rows), or no difference at all. The instrument also misses the one real head-loss line (`water chestnuts` → `water`). This is the instrument's largest bucket and it is what the report uses to re-attribute P12.16 ("+ `lemon peel only` + `2% milk` + `hard-cooked eggs`" — `2% milk` keyHead is `milk reduced fat fluid milkfat …` and `hard-cooked eggs` keyHead `egg whole`; neither lost a head word). Minimal fix: fire `compound-head-lost` only when a singularised `keyHeadPhrase[1:]` token appears among the normalised rawText tokens (keeps the §2 bread-crumbs line firing; `Flour`/boiled-egg/beef fall through to the brief's later classes). Command that shows it: `dotnet run --project tools/LetUsCook.AutoWrongCensus -- census /tmp/p1213-falsify/edge.jsonl` (Experiment 4) and the per-row scan of `autowrong-batch.tsv` (Experiment 5).

**2. `report-only` — the P12.16 water-chestnuts sentence is wrong for one of the two lines.** It says both lines' "rawText is a can unit" and both are "routed to `pack-unit-state × override`"; recorded TSV: `cashew-chicken-ii` = `pack-unit-state × override` (8-ounce can), `crab-stuffed-mushrooms-ii` = `sibling-food × override` with rawText `1/4 cup chopped water chestnuts` (no pack unit), and both lines' `keyHead` is `waterchestnut chinese` (two tokens, not the "single token" the report states).

**3. `tests` — three mutation survivors.** M3 (pack-unit key-Canned term), M12 (the `(` fold that the report says "replicates `FdcMatcher.StripFromParenthesis`" — parity is proven only by a comment; no test distinguishes it), M17 (`TierRank` order — no test pins the `key higher`/`accepted higher` split, nor any of the `overrideKey yes=`, `ShouldReuse … =false:`, or `missingField` summary lines; `grep -rn 'key higher' tools/LetUsCook.AutoWrongCensus.Tests` → no matches). Production code as shipped is correct on these (probes green on unmutated code; recorded summaries match the brief's tier order), so class `tests`.

Claims 1 (counts), 2 (three §2 lines — verified verbatim in the fresh TSV with the exact masks), 4 (guards), 5 (pairs 44 rows, byte-identical), and 6 (matrices/summaries match fresh re-run) hold; the commands in Experiments 1–3 are the ones that would have caught a break in each. Claim 3's "no re-implemented … head logic" is false in substance: the census-local `KeyHeadPhrase`/`CarriesStateToken` head definition is hand-rolled (disclosed in the report), and it is exactly where the instrument breaks (Finding 1). Scope checks pass: the only `src/` change is the two `InternalsVisibleTo` entries (commit stat), `grep -c AutoWrongCensus LetUsCook.slnx` = 2, no `tools/gates/f-425/` or `holdout-expected/` paths in either commit, tree clean, nothing committed.

**NO-GO class:** work

NO-GO (work) — first rejection. The falsifier's core finding is that my `compound-head-lost` rule fires on *any* single-token parsed name against a multi-token key description, so the bucket measures key-description shape, not head loss. **Commit:** `0dfc64154` (rework pending commit) · **Files:** 20 · **Elapsed:** ~300 min

## What changed
A new C# CLI instrument, `tools/LetUsCook.AutoWrongCensus` (Generic Host, Replay-shaped), classifies
**every** `auto == true && correct == false` line of a debug or batch trace into exactly one accepted-vs-key
relation (`pack-unit-state`, `compound-head-lost`, `state-mismatch`, `sibling-food`, `row-choice-tier`,
`same-head-other-qualifier`, `no-label`, `other`) and exactly one decision site (`override`, `reuse`,
`ranker`, `curated`), using **only** production helpers — `FdcNormalizer.NormalizeToTokens`,
`FdcMatcher.ExtractCandidateState`/`ExtractCandidateSatisfiers`, `FdcDescriptionParser.Parse(...).HeadTerm`,
`IngredientLineResolver.SingularizeToken` — reached via two `InternalsVisibleTo` entries in
`src/LetUsCook.Fdc/LetUsCook.Fdc.csproj` (the only `src` change). `census <trace.jsonl>` writes the full
TSV (header + one row per auto-wrong line) to stdout and the relation × site matrix, `other` rate,
missing-field counts, `overrideKey` yes/no, the `ShouldReuse(parsedName, linkedIngredientId)=false` count
and per-line qualifier diffs to stderr; it refuses any set other than `debug`|`batch` (D-029) before
writing anything. A second subcommand, `pairs <census.tsv> <trace.jsonl>`, emits the joined
window/`compound|other` table (5 columns) that P12.18 consumes. This is an instrument: it removes no
error and predicts nothing; it makes the auto-wrong buckets countable.

`compound-head-lost` additionally requires **head-tail evidence in rawText**: at least one token of the
key's head phrase beyond its first word must occur (singularised) in the normalised rawText. Without it
the bucket degenerates to "parsed name is one word and the key description is wordy" — the falsifier's
NO-GO-1 finding 1 ("2 cups flour" is not a lost "flour wheat"; 27/29 batch and 5/16 debug rows of the
first build had no lost head at all).

  first token for which production state/satisfier extraction is non-empty, each singularized by
